title: Level at Palmares
title_candidates: Two Forty-Sevens and a Vacated Lead
Thirty Holes in Front, Then Nothing
theme: A brand-new course hands out two career-shaping rounds and quietly removes David Mullin from the front of the TEG 10 Trophy, leaving Alex Baker and Gregg Williams dead level on 133 with one round to play.
opening_hook: David Mullin stood on the 18th tee at Palmares having just gone birdie, par, birdie — and walked off it with an eight, which was roughly the shape of his whole afternoon.

round_story.subject: Alex Baker and Gregg Williams both post 47 points on TEG's first visit to Palmares - Alvor / Lagos, arriving at the same number by conspicuously different routes
round_story.why_it_matters: Two rounds of the day, tied to the point, which is also why the TEG 10 Trophy now has two men on 133 and nothing separating them going into the final round.
round_story.shape: Alex Baker, playing a course nobody in the field had seen before, piles up 10 points across holes 2-4 and 9 more across 9-11; Gregg Williams grinds out the same 47 with a far tidier card, +15 gross against Alex Baker's +22. The turn is the 13th, where Alex Baker runs up a 10 and Gregg Williams makes a bogey for three points and briefly takes the Trophy lead outright. Both finish on 47 — a personal best for Alex Baker on both counts, and for Gregg Williams the second-best gross round of his TEG career — and both finish the day on 133.
headline_candidates: Alex Baker Posts His Best Round Yet
round_story.standfirst: Alex Baker's 47 is the best round of his TEG career and came with a 10 at the 13th; Gregg Williams matched it with seven fewer gross shots and no disasters at all.

race_story.subject: David Mullin's 31-point round ends 30 holes of Trophy leadership and drops him 11 behind, even as he retains the TEG 10 Green Jacket lead
race_story.why_it_matters: The man who had led the TEG 10 Trophy since the 12th hole of round one no longer leads it, and the race he does still lead has shrunk from 13 shots to 10.
race_story.shape: David Mullin had been in front of the Trophy continuously since the 12th hole of the first round, and was still level at the top after the 7th at Palmares. He lost the lead to Alex Baker at the 6th and never got it back, and although birdie, par, birdie at 15, 16 and 17 briefly suggested a rescue, a quadruple-bogey eight at the last closed the round at 31 points — 11 fewer than his second round. He ends the day third on 122, 11 adrift of the two men tied on 133, but still ahead in the Green Jacket on +38 with Jon Baker 10 back.
headline_candidates: Mullin's Thirty-Hole Lead Ends at Palmares
Mullin Loses One Race, Holds Another
race_story.chosen_headline: Mullin's Thirty-Hole Lead Ends at Palmares
race_story.standfirst: Three under for holes 15 to 17 counted for nothing once the 18th produced an eight, and the Green Jacket cushion is down from 13 to 10.

discovered_storylines.subject: John Patterson's round falls apart over holes 11 to 15 and pushes him 14 points clear at the foot of the TEG 10 Wooden Spoon
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: He began the day five points off the field and ends it 14 adrift, having lost 19 gross shots in five holes.
discovered_storylines.shape: John Patterson opened bogey, par, par for nine points across the first three holes and gave every impression of a man enjoying a new course, before a 10 at the par-five 8th put the first dent in it. From the 11th to the 15th he dropped 19 shots and did not make a single net par — an eight at the par-three 12th, a seven at the par-three 14th, a nine at the 15th. The round closed on 27 points and 108 gross, and the gap between him and the rest of the Wooden Spoon field went from five to 14.
headline_candidates: Patterson Loses Nineteen Shots in Five Holes
Five Holes That Settled the Spoon
No Net Pars From Eleven to Fifteen
discovered_storylines.chosen_headline: Patterson Loses Nineteen Shots in Five Holes
discovered_storylines.standfirst: Nine points from the opening three holes suggested one kind of day; an eight at a par three and a nine at the 15th supplied another.

race_state_note: The Trophy is tied at 133 with one round to play and TEG has no countback and no tiebreaker, so a level finish stays level; David Mullin remains ahead in the Green Jacket on gross, which measures something different from the Stableford table above it.
